originals.why: Here 'yn barod' is the predicate 'ready' (she's not ready), not the adverb 'already' that this LEGO teaches.

originals.ko: 나는 내가 이미 얼마나 많이 배웠는지 놀라워
나는 내가 이미 배운 것으로 행복해
너 내 형제를 기다릴 준비가 됐어?
originals.why: Uses 'barod i' meaning 'ready to', not 'yn barod' meaning 'already'. Wrong sense for this LEGO.
'yn barod i fynd' means 'ready to go', not 'already'. Wrong sense.

originals.ko: 하지만 너 제때 준비가 될 거야?
originals.why: 'fyddi di'n barod' means 'will you be ready', not 'already'. Wrong sense.

originals.ko: 너는 네가 준비가 될 거라고 생각해?
originals.why: 'yn barod' here means 'ready', not 'already'. Wrong sense.

originals.ko: 나는 내가 거의 준비가 됐다고 생각해
originals.why: 'bron yn barod' means 'nearly ready', not 'already'. Wrong sense.

originals.ko: 미안해 하지만 나는 나중에 준비가 될 거야
originals.why: 'fydda i'n barod' means 'I'll be ready', not 'already'. Wrong sense.

originals.ko: 너 내일 오후에 내 어머니를 도울 준비가 될 거야?
originals.why: 'barod i helpu' means 'ready to help', not 'already'. Wrong sense.

originals.ko: 너 준비 사항들을 도와줄 준비가 될 거야?
originals.why: 'barod i helpu' means 'ready to help', not 'already'. Wrong sense.
